title: Jazz players behind Sinatra and his musicianship
summary: Willard asks about jazz players with Sinatra; Tizol names Sweets and finds Sinatra a good musician with a fine ear.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Were there other musicians from the jazz world also working for Frank? I know he usually likes to have jazz musicians in the orchestra. I know he's used John Collins, Al Viola, and he used to have Ziggy Elman and Dave Barber and Herbie Hamer -- he had a lot of jazz musicians backing him. Were there other jazz people from jazz when you were working with him?

Well, when we worked with Sinatra, the band didn't do much, unless once in awhile, somebody had to take a little extra chorus, because Sinatra did the singing, and naturally, he didn't need anyone to back him up on something where he was playing a solo. The only one he used to once in awhile play something in the same recording was Sweets -- the trumpet player.
He used Earl Palmer on drums sometimes I know; I was at a recording session once where Earl Palmer was his drummer, but he usually uses Irv Kotler, doesn't he?
I don't know him. I mean, I don't remember.
What do you think of Sinatra's musicianship?

Oh, he directed the whole thing that we did with that woman -- oh, what's her name? She's very fat now. A very good singer. Oh, we did a terrific record together, and he directed the whole band and we had, I don't know how many fiddles and everything. We made a terrific record.
He has a pretty good ear, doesn't he?
Oh, yeah. He knows what he wants. He was nice to me.
